name: Ultrasound scaler (home)
lead: A home ultrasonic scaler is a consumer version of the vibrating instrument that dental professionals use to remove calculus (tartar), plaque and stain from teeth. Users in appearance communities discuss it as a way to remove tartar at home.

Published research on ultrasonic scaling concerns professional devices. Wikipedia describes them as electric tools that vibrate at high frequency and use a water spray to cool the tip and flush debris, and notes that research differs on whether they match hand instruments in effectiveness.[1] No studies of home-use scalers were found.

paras: Professional ultrasonic scalers vibrate at high frequency to loosen deposits, produce cavitation bubbles, and irrigate with liquid that cools the tip and rinses debris.[1] Two ultrasonic vibration systems exist, magnetostrictive and piezoelectric.[1] Clinicians often follow ultrasonic scaling with hand instruments.[1]
An American Academy of Periodontology position paper addresses sonic and ultrasonic scalers in periodontics.[2]

No studies found of home-use scalers. Laboratory studies of professional piezoelectric scalers have measured root substance removal in vitro, finding that working parameters such as lateral force, tip angle, power and time affect the amount removed.[3] An in vitro comparison of instruments also examined root substance loss in scaling.[4]

Ultrasonic scaling produces aerosol and splatter; a pilot study measured contamination distance and duration in a clinic setting.[5] Wikipedia lists possible damage to enamel cracks, early caries and resin restorations, and root surface sensitivity as risks of scaling in professional practice.[1]

card.summary: Consumer version of the dental ultrasonic scaler for tartar removal; research covers professional devices, not home units.
card.note: Research on enamel and root effects concerns professional use.

quick.overview:
A home ultrasonic scaler is a consumer tool modelled on the instrument dental hygienists use to remove tartar and stain.

Published work studies professional devices. No studies of home-use scalers were found.
quick.mechanism: Professional scalers vibrate at high frequency, loosen deposits and flush debris with a liquid spray.
quick.risks: Professional-setting research reports aerosol and splatter generation, and notes possible damage to enamel, restorations and root surfaces. Home-use safety data were not found.
